text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: 3xx node-group serving-runtime: multiple container crashes on gpu-pool-07; symptom: repeated CUDA illegal memory access / SIGSEGV during model reloads. Auto-escalation to incidents.
Nina K: seeing same in Grafana — 5xx spike and OOM kills starting ~08:12 UTC. Affected pods: runtime-{a,b,c} on gpu-07-3.
Samir P: I’m oncall, jumping in. Priority? customer-facing?
Carol S: Support - we’ve received 2 customer reports (org: finlytics, id: C-1034) with timeouts and error 503s. They say it started ~08:13 UTC.
Alex G: quick triage: nodes in question show kernel messages with "CUDA: illegal memory access" and then container restarts. Node flapping: kubelet evicting pods due to OOM then nodes go NotReady briefly.
Priya M: sharing extracted dmesg snippet from node gpu-07-3:
```
[  1234.567890] nv_peer_mem: fast mem remap fail at 0x7f8b...
[  1234.568012] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, PID=4321, GPU access fault, reason: illegal address
[  1234.568234] cuda_illegal_access: detected in /usr/bin/serving-runtime (pid 4321)
[  1234.569000] kernel: oom-killer invoked oom_score_adj=0
```
Nina K: good, that matches the container logs; paste from container stderr: 
```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what(): cuda: an illegal memory access was encountered
Aborted (core dumped)
```
Samir P: immediate mitigation options? cordon+drain node? fallback to CPU-only variants?
Alex G: recommend cordon gpu-07-3 and drain; also pause ongoing rollout (deploy-bot can do that). If this is a kernel/driver-level issue it may affect other nodes.
deploy-bot: Pause request acknowledged for rollout/serving-runtime@prod — canary halted.
Priya M: quick repro look: crashes happen during model hot-reload when kv-cache is resized. Could be race in our runtime + recent nv driver 535.x. We saw similar in lab with driver update.
Samir P: cordon/drain in progress. @Alex G, can you confirm no scheduled jobs will run on that node?
Alex G: cordoned gpu-07-3 (kubectl cordon gpu-07-3). Draining now: 
```
kubectl drain gpu-07-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```
Nina K: metrics update: 5xx rate down slightly after cordon, but still elevated. Some pods rescheduled to gpu-07-9 which has older driver.
Carol S: notifying impacted customers: sending templated message to Finlytics (brief update + ETA unknown).
Priya M: temporary mitigation: set RUNTIME_DISABLE_HOT_RELOAD=1 on pod spec and restart pods to avoid kv-cache resize path. That should avoid the vulnerable code path while we investigate.
Samir P: applying env change to the Deployment now (kubectl set env deployment/serving-runtime RUNTIME_DISABLE_HOT_RELOAD=1 --namespace prod). Will restart pods gradually.
Alex G: also collecting core dumps and gdb backtrace for crash PID 4321. Backtrace shows nvrtc-related call deep in driver memory copy during reload. Extract: 
```
#0  0x00007f8... in cudaMemcpyAsync 
#1  0x000056... in serving::KVCache::reload
#2  0x000056... in serving::Model::reload
```
Priya M: filing vendor ticket with NVIDIA. Attaching dmesg + core + driver version 535.54.03 + runtime build sha: abcdef123.
Samir P: what's the customer impact count? Carol?
Carol S: preliminary: 2 orgs reporting, 7 requests in SLO breach window, total ~1200 requests affected in last 15m. Marking P1 for now until we confirm containment.
Nina K: adding mitigations summary to incident doc: cordoned gpu-07-3, paused canary, disabled hot reload env var, restarted pods onto nodes with older driver where possible.
Priya M: long-term: patch runtime to add safer reload path + driver compatibility check at startup. Also schedule kernel/driver rollback for affected nodepool if vendor recommends.
Samir P: any risk of cascading to other pools? Alex?
Alex G: low but non-zero — we should proactively cordon nodes on pool where driver is 535.* and auto-schedule to nodes with 530.* until vendor confirms.
Samir P: doing proactive cordon for gpu-07-{0,1,2}. Will monitor.
Nina K: monitoring: set alert for "cuda_illegal_access" dmesg pattern + pod restarts; paging through logs shows increased page faults before crash — may indicate race under memory pressure.
Carol S: posting customer update: we’ve applied a temporary mitigation and scheduled a maintenance window if needed. Customer asked for ETA for full fix.
Priya M: ETA: hotpatch/runtime fix estimate 1-2 business days, vendor patch unknown. Will update after vendor response.
Samir P: opening incident ticket INC-2026-314, assigning leads: Samir (Incident Commander), Priya (Runtime), Alex (Infra), Carol (Customer comms).
Nina K: last check — errors trending down after env change, request success rate improving. Keeping this incident live for monitoring and postmortem.
Samir P: thanks all — if anything new, post here. Handing off to night oncall @Nina K in 30m.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-314 created and assigned. Timeline tracking enabled.
